acceptable_use_policy: Data is used for law enforcement purposes only. Data is owned by Auburn WA PD and is never sold to 3rd parties.
prohibited_uses: Immigration enforcement, traffic enforcement, harassment or intimidation, usage based solely on a protected class (i.e. race, sex, religion), Personal use.
access_policy: All system access requires a valid reason.
hotlist_policy: Hotlist hits are required to be human verified prior to action.
hotlists_alerted_on: Washington Crime Information Center (WACIC), NCMEC Amber Alert
sharing_outbound: Columbia River Drug Task Force WA
overview:
Auburn WA PD uses Flock Safety technology to capture objective evidence without compromising on individual privacy. Auburn WA PD utilizes retroactive search to solve crimes after they've occurred. Additionally, Auburn WA PD utilizes real time alerting of hotlist vehicles to capture wanted criminals. In an effort to ensure proper usage and guardrails are in place, they have made the below policies and usage statistics available to the public.

success_stories:
In the spring of 2025, Auburn Police responded to a call for service which resulted in a homicide investigation. During the investigation, APD personnel learned that a specific vehicle was used by the suspects to flee the scene. Using city owned camera footage, APD personnel managed to obtain some video of the suspect vehicle, but the clarity was limited, only allowing APD personnel to gather a general description of its make and model.

However, when APD personnel searched the Flock Safety Camera system in our city, a matching make and model was quickly located, which provided APD with a license plate number. By combining the information from the city owned camera systems with Flock, APD personnel were able to confirm the exact vehicle involved in the homicide. Within six hours, APD personnel entered the license plate into a WA State system as a Be On the Look Out (BOLO) for the awareness of all law enforcement.

Later that day, an officer from an outside agency found the suspect vehicle abandoned on the side of the road. Thanks to the quick identification of the vehicle, APD personnel were able to collect very valuable evidence. This success would not have been possible without Flock. The suspect in the homicide was later arrested and booked into jail.

In June of 2026, an Auburn PD officer conducted a preliminary investigation of a vehicle prowl incident. During that investigation, the officer attempted to conduct a traffic stop on a vehicle to interview the driver and sole occupant. The vehicle fled and the officer made the appropriate decision to self-terminate the vehicle pursuit due to the risk posed by the driver's actions but was able to articulate the crime of attempting to elude a police vehicle, a class C felony.

Within hours on the same day, the officer was able to use Flock to locate the vehicle in the Covington area. While preparing the vehicle for impound and evidence processing, the officer noticed the driver walking in the area and contacted him. The driver was subsequently arrested and booked into jail. A search warrant was executed on the vehicle, and a loaded firearm was located inside. The driver's criminal history contains numerous felony convictions. This is an example of fantastic police work involving great decision making by the officer. What initially appeared to be a low-level property crime, quickly escalated into a dangerous incident. In this incident, Flock significantly enhanced the ability of law enforcement to provide efficient resolution to a criminal case involving a firearm and holding a subject accountable according to the law.
